lesson_1.topicLabel: Enquiry 01: Secret Code in Place-Names and Old Ordnance Survey Maps
lesson_1.title: How do place-names and old maps unlock secret history on our doorstep?
lesson_1.spokenTitle: How do place-names and old maps unlock secret history on our doorstep?

cards.heading: Cracking Place-Name Endings
cards.connective: How do place-names and old maps unlock secret history on our doorstep?
cards.html: Roman castra (-chester), Saxon farms (-ton, -ham), and Viking villages (-by) hide ancient settler clues preserved in the 1086 Domesday Book.
cards.spoken: How do place-names and old maps unlock secret history on our doorstep? <short pause> Roman castra (-chester), Saxon farms (-ton, -ham), and Viking villages (-by) hide ancient settler clues preserved in the 1086 Domesday Book.

cards.heading: 1880s Ordnance Survey Maps
cards.connective: Centuries later, scientific map-makers drew every street and field.
cards.html: Comparing 1880s Ordnance Survey sheets with modern maps reveals vanished mills, lost railways, and green fields now beneath houses.
cards.spoken: Centuries later, scientific map-makers drew every street and field. <short pause> Comparing 1880s Ordnance Survey sheets with modern maps reveals vanished mills, lost railways, and green fields now beneath houses.

cards.heading: Stone Benchmarks & Trig Pillars
cards.connective: Surveyors also left permanent stone and concrete clues outdoors.
cards.html: Chiseled broad-arrow benchmarks on old walls mark sea-level heights, while 1936 hilltop trig pillars sighted map triangles.
cards.spoken: Surveyors also left permanent stone and concrete clues outdoors. <short pause> Chiseled broad-arrow benchmarks on old walls mark sea-level heights, while 1936 hilltop trig pillars sighted map triangles.

cards.heading: Every Street Sign Tells a Story
cards.connective: Combining place-names and historic maps unlocks any British neighbourhood.
cards.html: Any UK pupil can decode settler endings, compare 1880s maps, and spot real Ordnance Survey marks outdoors.
cards.spoken: Combining place-names and historic maps unlocks any British neighbourhood. <short pause> Any UK pupil can decode settler endings, compare 1880s maps, and spot real Ordnance Survey marks outdoors.

lesson_1.takeaway: Place-name endings, the 1086 Domesday Book, 1880s Ordnance Survey maps, and carved benchmarks reveal over a thousand years of settlement on any UK doorstep.
vocab: 1. Castra
Latin for Roman fort; gives -chester and -caster town names.
2. Domesday Book
King William I’s 1086 survey naming 13,000+ places.
3. Ordnance Survey
Britain’s national mapping agency, founded in 1791.

lesson_2.topicLabel: Enquiry 02: Reading Buildings on the High Street — Timber, Brick and Royal Cyphers
lesson_2.title: How can timber frames, brickwork, and postboxes date a British street?
lesson_2.spokenTitle: How can timber frames, brickwork, and postboxes date a British street?

cards.heading: Tudor Timber & Jetties
cards.connective: How can timber frames, brickwork, and postboxes date a British street?
cards.html: Look above modern shop signs! Tudor buildings show dark oak timber frames, white wattle-and-daub panels, and overhanging upper jetties.
cards.spoken: How can timber frames, brickwork, and postboxes date a British street? <short pause> Look above modern shop signs! Tudor buildings show dark oak timber frames, white wattle-and-daub panels, and overhanging upper jetties.

cards.heading: Georgian Sash vs Victorian Brick
cards.connective: Brick, stone, and railway transport reshaped town streets.
cards.html: Georgian terraces lined up calm sliding sash windows, while Victorian railways brought fiery red brick and terracotta.
cards.spoken: Brick, stone, and railway transport reshaped town streets. <short pause> Georgian terraces lined up calm sliding sash windows, while Victorian railways brought fiery red brick and terracotta.

cards.heading: Cyphers, Datestones & Ghost Signs
cards.connective: Street furniture and painted brickwork pin down exact dates.
cards.html: Check red postboxes for Royal Cyphers (V.R., G.R., E.IIR), doorways for carved datestones, and brick gables for faded ghost signs.
cards.spoken: Street furniture and painted brickwork pin down exact dates. <short pause> Check red postboxes for Royal Cyphers (V.R., G.R., E.IIR), doorways for carved datestones, and brick gables for faded ghost signs.

cards.heading: A Living Timeline Above Our Heads
cards.connective: Every British high street mixes chapters from different centuries.
cards.html: Looking upwards turns any walk to the shops into a detective hunt across Tudor, Georgian, and Victorian Britain.
cards.spoken: Every British high street mixes chapters from different centuries. <short pause> Looking upwards turns any walk to the shops into a detective hunt across Tudor, Georgian, and Victorian Britain.

lesson_2.takeaway: Looking above modern shopfronts—and checking V.R. postboxes, datestones, and brick ghost signs—lets detectives date Tudor, Georgian, and Victorian streets anywhere in Britain.
vocab: 1. Jetty
Overhanging upper floor on a Tudor timber-framed house.
2. Sash Window
Tall sliding wooden window popular in Georgian terraces.
3. Royal Cypher
Monarch’s initials (like V.R. or E.IIR) on postboxes.

cards.connective: What can censuses, parish books, and school logbooks reveal about past families?

cards.spoken: What can censuses, parish books, and school logbooks reveal about past families? <short pause> Door-to-door enumerators listed every household’s ages, birthplaces, and vanished Victorian jobs like ostlers and lamplighters.

cards.heading: 1862 School Logbooks

cards.spoken: Locked inside school desks lay weekly diaries of childhood. <short pause> Victorian School Logbooks record autumn harvest absences, deep snowdrifts, shared boots, and sums on grey slates.

cards.heading: Meeting Ordinary Neighbours by Name

Official every-ten-year count of everyone living in Britain.
2. Enumerator
Local officer who walked door to door copying Census forms.

Stable worker who cared for horses at a coaching inn.

lesson_4.topicLabel: Enquiry 04: How Our Town Earned Its Living — Farms, Canals, Mills and Stations
lesson_4.title: How do street names, canals, mills, and stations show past local work?
lesson_4.spokenTitle: How do street names, canals, mills, and stations show past local work?

cards.heading: Market Crosses & Milestones
cards.connective: How do street names, canals, mills, and stations show past local work?
cards.html: Roofed market crosses sheltered farm stalls, while turnpike roads placed carved stone milestones and horse troughs along coach routes.
cards.spoken: How do street names, canals, mills, and stations show past local work? <short pause> Roofed market crosses sheltered farm stalls, while turnpike roads placed carved stone milestones and horse troughs along coach routes.

cards.heading: Waterwheels, Canals & Locks
cards.connective: Rivers and artificial canals powered Britain’s heavy goods boom.
cards.html: Streams turned mill waterwheels, and towpath horses pulled narrowboats of coal and china through wooden canal locks.
cards.spoken: Rivers and artificial canals powered Britain’s heavy goods boom. <short pause> Streams turned mill waterwheels, and towpath horses pulled narrowboats of coal and china through wooden canal locks.

cards.heading: Steam Stations & Street Clues
cards.connective: Railways linked every town—and left clues even where lines closed.
cards.html: Victorian steam railways sped milk and coal into red-brick stations, echoed today in cycle paths, Station Road, and Mill Lane signs.
cards.spoken: Railways linked every town—and left clues even where lines closed. <short pause> Victorian steam railways sped milk and coal into red-brick stations, echoed today in cycle paths, Station Road, and Mill Lane signs.

cards.heading: Landscape Clues to Everyday Work
cards.connective: Every bridge, wharf, and street sign explains how a town grew.
cards.html: Tracing milestones, locks, mills, and street names reveals how communities across Britain earned their living.
cards.spoken: Every bridge, wharf, and street sign explains how a town grew. <short pause> Tracing milestones, locks, mills, and street names reveals how communities across Britain earned their living.

lesson_4.takeaway: Market halls, turnpike milestones, canal locks, watermills, steam stations, and street names like Mill Lane or Station Road reveal how any UK town earned its living.
vocab: 1. Turnpike
18th-century toll road marked with carved stone milestones.
2. Milestone
Roadside stone or iron post showing miles to nearby towns.
3. Canal Lock
Water chamber with gates lifting narrowboats up hills.

lesson_5.topicLabel: Enquiry 05: Names Carved in Stone — Local War Memorials and Commonwealth Records

cards.heading: 100,000+ Local War Memorials
cards.connective: How can War Memorials and Commonwealth records trace one local soldier’s story?
cards.html: Because graves lay overseas, every town and village carved local surnames—often brothers side by side—onto stone crosses honoured with poppies.
cards.spoken: How can War Memorials and Commonwealth records trace one local soldier’s story? <short pause> Because graves lay overseas, every town and village carved local surnames—often brothers side by side—onto stone crosses honoured with poppies.

cards.heading: 1917 Equal White Headstones
cards.stat: Sir Fabian Ware • White Portland Stone
cards.connective: Overseas cemeteries broke with class division forever.
cards.html: Founded in 1917 by Fabian Ware, War Graves cemeteries gave generals and teenage privates identical white Portland stone headstones.
cards.spoken: Overseas cemeteries broke with class division forever. <short pause> Founded in 1917 by Fabian Ware, War Graves cemeteries gave generals and teenage privates identical white Portland stone headstones.

cards.heading: From Stone Cross to Home Street
cards.connective: Four archives reconnect a carved surname to a real childhood home.
cards.html: Matching free CWGC registers, bronze Memorial Plaques, medals, and the 1911 Census traces one soldier back to a local street.
cards.spoken: Four archives reconnect a carved surname to a real childhood home. <short pause> Matching free CWGC registers, bronze Memorial Plaques, medals, and the 1911 Census traces one soldier back to a local street.

cards.heading: World History on One Local Street
cards.stat: Every Carved Name Was a Neighbour
cards.connective: Local memorials link giant world events to real families next door.
cards.html: Respectful detective work turns carved stone initials back into real sons, daughters, and neighbours.
cards.spoken: Local memorials link giant world events to real families next door. <short pause> Respectful detective work turns carved stone initials back into real sons, daughters, and neighbours.

lesson_5.takeaway: Local War Memorials, Sir Fabian Ware’s equal 1917 Portland stone headstones, bronze plaques, and the 1911 Census let pupils trace one carved name back to a real street.

Local monument carved with names of neighbours who died in war.
2. Cenotaph
Monument ("empty tomb") honouring those buried far away.
3. Portland Stone
White Dorset limestone used for equal CWGC headstones.
